name: Belueli
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Schebesta, Paul. 1953. Die Belueli vom Apare (Ituri). Kongo-Overzee 19(4): 357-375.
catalog_locator: p. 367, section 'Das Belueli-Idiom' (page number 367 on the page; = archive.org)
catalog_quote: Die Beluelisprache arbeitet wie die Nachbarsprachen alle mit musikalischen Tönen, die soweit ich sehe die nämlichen sind wie bei den anderen Stämmen. Ich notierte einen Hochton (á) [ˊ] Akzent (aigu) über dem Vokal, einen mittleren Sington (ā) [-]; dieser mittlere Sington wird bisweilen Sing-Hochton, ausnahmsweise mit zwei Akzenten (a̋) angedeutet, und einem Tiefton (à) (grave) [_] über dem Vokal. ɛ und ɔ sind die offenen Vokale. Zahlreich sind die Intermediärvokale zwischen e/i (ẹ) und o/u (ọ), die ich aber hier nicht weiter kennzeichne. Das l ist immer lateral; r und reines l kommen nicht vor.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Die Beluelisprache arbeitet wie die Nachbarsprachen alle mit musikalischen Tönen, die soweit ich sehe die nämlichen sind wie bei den anderen Stämmen. Ich notierte einen Hochton (á) [ˊ] Akzent (aigu) über dem Vokal, einen mittleren Sington (ā) [-]; dieser mittlere Sington wird bisweilen Sing-Hochton, ausnahmsweise mit zwei Akzenten (a̋) angedeutet, und einem Tiefton (à) (grave) [_] über dem Vokal.
new_statements.translation: The Belueli language, like all the neighbouring languages, works with musical tones, which as far as I can see are the same as among the other tribes. I noted a high tone (á), an acute accent over the vowel; a mid level tone (ā) [-]; this mid level tone sometimes becomes a level-high tone, exceptionally indicated with two accents (a̋); and a low tone (à) (grave) [_] over the vowel.
new_statements.citation: Schebesta, Paul. 1953. Die Belueli vom Apare (Ituri). Kongo-Overzee 19(4): 357-375.
new_statements.locator: p. 367, section 'Das Belueli-Idiom' (p. 11 of the extract; p. 81 of the whole-issue scan)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (19 pp., scanned text present, no scanned needed). p.11 carries the printed page number 367 and is the same page as p.81 of the whole-issue scan checked: 'musikalischen Toenen' on p.81 of that file). Rendered p.11 at 150 dpi and the tone paragraph at 300 dpi: the quoted passage 'Die Beluelisprache arbeitet wie die Nachbarsprachen alle mit musikalischen Toenen, die soweit ich sehe die naemlichen sind wie bei den anderen Staemmen. Ich notierte einen Hochton (a) [.] Akzent (aigu) ueber dem Vokal, einen mittleren Sington (a) [-]; dieser mittlere Sington wird bisweilen Sing-Hochton, ausnahmsweise mit zwei Akzenten (a) angedeutet, und einem Tiefton (a) (grave) [_] ueber dem Vokal.' is ther…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only description states that Belueli is a tone language with three noted levels (high, mid, low, plus an occasional 'level-high' variant of the mid tone), the same system as its neighbours; nothing at all is said about word stress or prominence, and the word 'Akzent' is used only as the name of the acute diacritic.
new_statements.exceptions: None about stress. Schebesta notes that pronunciation varied from speaker to speaker (p. 368) and that the data were fixed with several informants who often contradicted each other (p. 366); the class-prefix system was collapsing.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the language as a whole (tones on vowels of cited words and short texts); citation-form elicitation from semi-speakers in 1929 and 1950 of a language the author calls dead ('Das Belueli ist heute eine tote Sprache', p. 367). The diacritic glyphs in the quote are transcribed from the microfilm page scan; the double-accent symbol is rendered as a̋ (two acutes) per the text 'mit zwei Akzenten'.
new_statements.identity_note: Schebesta 1953 describes the idiom of the Belueli, a group of 200-300 'village pygmies' (Basua wa mungine, called Balioli by the Bakango pygmies and Bapali by the Babali) at the Apare river on the Bafwasende-Bomili road; = Glottolog belu1239 (hh record: 'Belueli ca 27.2 E 1.4 N = Basua = Balioli', not intelligible to Bali bcp). The data were elicited in 1929 and 1950 from semi-speakers; Schebesta states the language was already dead in daily use by 1950 (p.367), and the group now speaks Bali (bali1274 / bcp). Only classification note in Glottolog: Nyali-Ndaka-Mbo-Budu-Vanuma subgroup; Kutsch Lojenga 2003 pp.450-452 and Rasmussen 2018 (both held held by the project) do not name Belueli.

sources.note: Section 'Das Belueli-Idiom' pp.366-375; phonology paragraph p.367: the language 'works with musical tones' like its neighbours — high tone (acute), mid 'Sington' (macron, sometimes rising to high, exceptionally marked with two acutes), low tone (grave); no mention of stress/Betonung at all ('Akzent' used only as the name of the diacritic). Verified against the page scan (p.11 of the extract = journal p.367).

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Pages 450-452 discuss the two D30 groupings (Budu-Ndaka-Mbo-Nyali-Vanuma vs Amba-Bira-Bhele-Bila-Kaiku-Kango-Komo) and say the affiliation of Bali and Lika is unclear; Belueli is not mentioned; the phonology is of Bila (three tone levels, downstep), not Belueli.
